us-hhs-2026-peptide-policy.summary: US compounding of six peptides: brought up to date with the draft HHS policy of 30 October 2026.
us-hhs-2026-peptide-policy.detail: These pages said that compounding BPC-157, TB-500, KPV, MOTS-c, Semax and epitalon in the US stays prohibited until the FDA completes a rule. On 30 October 2026 the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) published a draft policy: until a final rule decides on each, HHS does not intend to take enforcement action against pharmacies, federal facilities or licensed doctors that compound them under strict conditions. The pages now say so. The law has not changed: none of the six is on the 503A list, and on 3 November 2026 no rule had been proposed. The policy is not binding, approves nothing and changes nothing outside the US. Sources: the Federal Register notice FR Doc. 2026-22192 and the HHS policy.

tesamorelin-approval-answer.summary: Tesamorelin: “Is it an approved medicine?” now answers for each country, with the US approval and Canada’s.
tesamorelin-approval-answer.detail: Before, the answer started with the EU status and did not name the US, where tesamorelin has been an approved medicine since 10 November 2010. It also left out Canada. It now answers for each country: approved in the US; approved in Canada on 29 April 2014, but the company stopped selling it there on 30 September 2022; not approved in the UK or Australia. The dates come from the FDA and Health Canada and are shown, with their sources, in the status table on the page.
